enumeration.method: Independent bold-heading enumeration and visual comparison of all ten theorem statements.

source_notes.note: T3.2 and T4.1 import the conclusion of T3.1 with design/kernel replacements, not its high-entropy assumptions. T5.1(i) assumes the conclusion of T3.1; T5.1(ii) and T5.3 import T3.2 assumptions. T5.2 imports (9) only; T5.4 imports T4.1 assumptions and (14) only. Preserve these distinctions.

Fixed-H uses Assumptions 1,6–8; growing-H uses 1,8–11. The union in a theorem dependency inventory denotes use in different branches, not simultaneous hypotheses. Theta references in growing-H Table 3 do not impose Assumption 10 on fixed-H formulas.
Quantile paths D are left continuous with right limits and ball sigma-field. Right-continuous tilde-D is a proof empirical-process space, not the inventoried quantile-process state space.

Assumptions 2 and 10 quantify over arbitrary p1,...,pk without saying distinct. Repeated indices duplicate coordinates and conflict with strict positive definiteness. Preserve the printed quantifiers; no inferred distinctness is inserted.

Equation (8), Gamma_h and Table 2 visually place expectation immediately on the first centered factor, without explicit outer parentheses enclosing the product. The intended covariance grouping is an inference. Original formulas retain the printed placement.

E_P(X_i)^2 in Table 1, Table 2 and Table 3 can be misread as squared mean rather than second moment. The regression estimator slope suggests the latter interpretation. E_P(X_i)^(-1) similarly uses a trailing power in inverse-moment assumptions. Preserve typography rather than silently reparenthesize.
Bar-X occurs in (7) and (13), but no explicit main-text defining equation was found. Interpreting it as the known finite-population auxiliary mean is plausible, not a quoted definition.

Zeta-hat and stratified zeta-hat substitute estimators from supplement Tables 5 and 6. Exact density/moment substitutions are not supplied in the main text. The references remain unresolved; no supplement or appendix body was read.

Rejective sampling and piPS are named with external references; main text provides the KL characterization of high entropy and the full RHC grouping procedure, but not full rejective/piPS construction formulas. Do not invent them.

Section 6.2 names and cites the GREG mean estimator without specifying its formula. This is not automatically the uncentered quantile regression coefficient in (2). Main-text census keeps it unresolved.

T6.1 and T6.2 refer to asymptotic covariance kernels in preceding prose but omit Assumption 3 and the W second-moment hypothesis in their printed opening conditions. Record that existence/regularity gap without adding those hypotheses to the quotation or dependency graph.

T6.3 comparisons are separately paired by respectively. The surrounding paragraph centers at superpopulation mean/median, not finite-population targets. Variance/correlation existence is implicit rather than explicitly guaranteed by printed Assumptions 1 and 3.

Equations (23) and (24) print 1/4 f_y^2 and 1/4 sigma_y^2 f_y^2 in slash notation. Interpreting the full products as denominators is inferred from context; original statement preserves the slash form.
Table 2 superscript 1 and Table 3 superscript 2 are footnote marks; in Table 3 the repeated mark preceding Theta is neither exponent nor multiplication by 2.

J and f are described as smooth, without a numeric order. The variance estimator gradient is evaluated at Qhat_y, not an arbitrary adjusted G, as printed. Theorem 5.1 uses a limiting finite-population gradient; comparison theorems write the superpopulation gradient directly.

recorded_checks: Ten complete main-text Theorems, numbered 3.1,3.2,4.1,5.1–5.4,6.1–6.3; Theorem 6.2 continues across pages 23–24. All bold headings enumerated independently through the clipped main-text endpoint on page 29.

Thirty-seven source entries and fourteen supporting passages preserve four estimators, design and probability conventions, all eleven assumptions, both Table 3 regimes, all covariance/plug-in formulas and the externally named GREG mean estimator.

Independent graph reconstruction confirms 122 direct uses and 171 related connections. Conclusion references do not import sufficient hypotheses. Fixed-H and growing-H alternatives are explicitly described separately. Comparison kernels do not acquire an unprinted Assumption 3 through notation.

Normalized sample CDF and uncentered regression slope are preserved. Quantile paths are left continuous. Table 3 footnote marks remain distinct from powers. Table 2 and equation (8) retain expectation placement, and Theorem 6.3 preserves slash division and separate respectively comparisons.

The exact plug-in substitutions are referred to supplement Tables 5 and 6; rejective/piPS constructions and GREG are externally cited; bar-X lacks an explicit main-text defining equation. These are recorded as unresolved, without reading appendices or supplying standard replacements.

Fifteen source scope/convention issues explicitly document branch scope, repeated-index positive definiteness, expectation/moment typography, missing comparison regularity premises, superpopulation centering and implicit correlation existence. No source statement is silently repaired.

Every entry uses literal source terms, appropriate source kind and heading, and source-backed selectors. All 171 relationships have paper-local explanation paths with the relevant subpart/design scope.

All six content JSON artifacts regenerate byte for byte using the retained per-paper scripts. Frozen content hashes, independent PDF heading enumeration, source-specific checks, dependency reconstruction and schema validation pass.
